topIssues.title: op-node: reactive runtime config reload on unsafe block signer mismatch
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Problem

When the unsafe block signer address is rotated in the L1 `SystemConfig` contract, op-node verifier nodes experience a **stale signer window** during which they reject valid blocks from the new signer.

The unsafe block signer is loaded as a **runtime config** — it's explicitly excluded from derivation ([`system_config.go:142-144`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80b646e794/op-node/rollup/derive/system_config.go#L142-L144)) and instead fetched by a **periodic background reload loop** ([`node.go:454-487`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80b646e794/op-node/node/node.go#L454-L487)) that reads the value from L1 contract storage (`eth_getStorageAt`) at a configurable interval (default: **10 minutes**).

During gossip validation, the block signature is checked against the currently loaded signer address ([`gossip.go:445-463`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80b646e794/op-node/p2p/gossip.go#L445-L463)). If the signer was rotated on L1 but the node hasn't reloaded yet, blocks signed by the **new legitimate signer are rejected**.

Worst-case activation delay: `VerifierConfDepth × L1 block time + reload interval` ≈ **~11 minutes** with defaults.

During this window:
- Blocks from the new (legitimate) signer are rejected
- Blocks from the old signer continue to be accepted
- The node falls behind on the unsafe chain until the reload fires

## Proposed Solution

Add a **reactive reload mechanism**: when a gossip block fails signature verification, trigger an early runtime config reload (rate-limited to prevent abuse).

### Design

1. **Reload channel**: Pass a `chan struct{}` into `BuildBlocksValidator` alongside the existing `GossipRuntimeConfig`. On signature mismatch, send a non-blocking signal on this channel.

2. **Rate limiting**: The reloader goroutine in `initRuntimeConfig` consumes from this channel but enforces a **minimum cooldown** (e.g., 2 seconds) between reactive reloads to prevent L1 RPC abuse from attacker-crafted invalid blocks.

3. **Confirmation depth**: Reactive reloads still apply `VerifierConfDepth` — the signer rotation should be timed so that the L1 update is confirmed before the sequencers switch over.

4. **Validation result**: Use `pubsub.ValidationIgnore` instead of `pubsub.ValidationReject` when triggering a reactive reload, so the peer is not penalized for a potentially legitimate signer rotation.

This reduces worst-case activation delay to `VerifierConfDepth × L1 block time + 2s cooldown`.

### Future improvement: per-peer grace window

A more nuanced approach would track per-peer invalid signature counts and allow each peer a small number (e.g., 3) of `ValidationIgnore` responses before escalating to `ValidationReject`. This would:

- Avoid penalizing honest peers during a signer rotation
- Still penalize peers that persistently send invalid signatures
- Reset the counter when the signer address changes (detected via `P2PSequencerAddress()`)

This could use an LRU cache of `peer.ID → count`, purged on signer change, similar to the existing `seenBlocks` pattern. This is left as a follow-up to keep the initial implementation simple.

But this may be more complex than necessary. Maybe we just put this behavior behind a `--expect-unsafe-signer-change` and only enable reactive runtime config reloading if this parameter is active, and only then use `ValidationIgnore` instead of `ValidationReject`.

🤖 *Generated by Claude Code and Seb (human)*

topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestExecutePayloadSuccess`
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Flaky Test

**Test:** `TestExecutePayloadSuccess`
**Package:** `rust/op-reth/tests/proofs/core`
**CI Job:** `op-reth-e2e-sysgo-tests`

## CI Runs

- https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/121652/workflows/c7a2af02-affc-4d0d-bd43-461f58d6a244/jobs/4731572
- Failed 2 times in a row with the same error

## Error

```
execute_payload_test.go:61: no state found for block number 1
```

## Context

The test sets up a system, funds an account (tx confirmed at block 1), then immediately queries op-reth for the state of block 1. op-reth doesn't have the state ready yet — likely a race condition between block production and state availability in the execution client.

Two other proof tests in the same package pass consistently (`TestL2MultipleTransactionsInDifferentBlocks`, `TestL2MultipleTransactionsInSingleBlock`).

Encountered while working on ethereum-optimism/optimism#19881.

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth): in-memory overlay state with async persistence [WIP]
topPRs.author: dhyaniarun1993
topPRs.body:
# Description

**Summary**

Replaces the direct-to-disk write path in `LiveTrieCollector` with a write-buffer architecture. Blocks are now accumulated in an in-memory buffer and flushed to disk asynchronously by a dedicated persistence service. An overlay provider allows block execution to read from buffered state that hasn't been persisted yet, decoupling execution throughput from disk I/O latency.

** Motivation**

Previously, every call to `execute_and_store_block_updates` or `store_block_updates` opened a read-write transaction, wrote the diff, and committed synchronously. This made block processing throughput directly bottlenecked by disk write speed. 

This PR:
- Decouples block execution from disk writes, so the ExEx can process blocks at EVM speed while I/O happens in the background
- Batches multiple block diffs into a single write transaction, reducing transaction overhead
- Moves pruning into the same write transaction as persistence, eliminating the separate prune task and its race window
- Introduces backpressure so the buffer doesn't grow unbounded if persistence falls behind

Architecture
```
ExEx loop ──► LiveTrieCollector (in-memory buffer)
                  │
                  │ advance_persistence() when buffer ≥ threshold
                  ▼
              std::thread::spawn ──► LiveTriePersistenceHandle
                                         │
                                         │ crossbeam channel
                                         ▼
                                    LiveTriePersistenceService (background thread)
                                         │
                                         ├─ batch write (store_trie_updates_batch)
                                         ├─ prune (prune_with_provider)
                                         └─ commit
```

**Tests**

Pending

**Additional context**

NA

**Metadata**

Blocked on https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19928

# Notes 

We should refactor(this or another PR) LiveTrieCollector into an engine:
- LiveTrieCollectorEngine — a private struct that owns all mutable state and runs a single-threaded message loop on a dedicated thread. Processes a CollectorAction enum (ExecuteAndStore, StoreBlockUpdates, UnwindAndStore, UnwindHistory, WaitForPersistence, GetTipBlockNumber) sequentially, structurally enforcing the serial-call invariant.
- LiveTrieCollectorHandle — a thin, clonable Sender<CollectorAction> wrapper that is the only public type. Every method sends a message + blocks on a one-shot reply channel, preserving the existing synchronous API.

This eliminates:
- `PersistenceStatus` (Mutex + Condvar) — persistence tracking becomes engine-local (persist_in_flight: bool + persist_reply_rx: Option<Receiver>)
- parking_lot dependency from this module
- Throwaway `std::thread::spawn` per flush — the engine sends directly to the persistence service

topPRs.title: interop: add OPContractsManagerMigrationValidator for post-migration validation
topPRs.author: stevennevins
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Add `OPContractsManagerMigrationValidator`, a new contract to validate L1 contract configuration after an interop migration (`opcm.migrate()`). This verifies that shared infrastructure (DGF, ASR, ETHLockbox, DelayedWETH) and per-chain cross-references are correctly set up.

Separated from `OPContractsManagerStandardValidator` due to EIP-170 contract size limits.

Closes #16033

## Details

Stacked on #19840.

### New entry points

- `validateMigration(MigrationValidationInput, bool)` — validates shared infra once + each chain
- `validateMigrationWithOverrides(...)` — same with `ValidationOverrides` support

### Current state

This PR adds the contract scaffold with stub implementations. Validation logic will be added incrementally.
